Background Human decidua basalis mesenchymal stem/multipotent stromal cells (DBMSCs) inhibit endothelial cell activation by inflammation induced by monocytes. This property makes them a promising candidate for cell-based therapy to treat inflammatory diseases, such as atherosclerosis. This study was performed to examine the ability of DBMSCs to protect endothelial cell functions from the damaging effects resulting from exposure to oxidatively stress environment induced by H 2 O 2 and monocytes. Methods DBMSCs were co-cultured with endothelial cells isolated from human umbilical cord veins in the presence of H 2 O 2 and monocytes, and various functions of endothelial cell were then determined. The effect of DBMSCs on monocyte adhesion to endothelial cells in the presence of H 2 O 2 was also examined. In addition, the effect of DBMSCs on HUVEC gene expression under the influence of H 2 O 2 was also determined. Results DBMSCs reversed the effect of H 2 O 2 on endothelial cell functions. In addition, DBMSCs reduced monocyte adhesion to endothelial cells and also reduced the stimulatory effect of monocytes on endothelial cell proliferation in the presence of H 2 O 2 . Moreover, DBMSCs modified the expression of many genes mediating important endothelial cell functions. Finally, DBMSCs increased the activities of glutathione and thioredoxin reductases in H 2 O 2 -treated endothelial cells. Conclusions We conclude that DBMSCs have potential for therapeutic application in inflammatory diseases, such as atherosclerosis by protecting endothelial cells from oxidative stress damage. However, more studies are needed to elucidate this further. extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated the ability of human decidua basalis mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (DBMSCs) to protect human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) from oxidative stress and inflammation induced by hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and monocytes. The research examined various endothelial cell functions, including proliferation, adhesion, and migration, alongside monocyte adhesion and proliferation, as well as the expression of adhesion molecules and antioxidant enzymes. The findings suggest DBMSCs possess therapeutic potential for inflammatory diseases like atherosclerosis by shielding endothelial cells from oxidative stress-induced damage.

treatment_details.therapy_type: In vitro co-culture with Human Decidua Basalis Mesenchymal Stem/Stromal Cells (DBMSCs)
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC, passages 3-5) were exposed to 100 µM H2O2 for 48 hours. DBMSCs (passage 3) were co-cultured with HUVEC using three distinct methods: conditioned medium (CMDBMSC, at 1%, 5%, and 25% v/v concentrations), secretome-free direct contact (SFDBMSC, via a transwell system), and intercellular direct contact (ICDBMSC). Co-culture ratios of HUVEC to DBMSC included 1:1, 5:1, and 10:1, with a 5HUVEC:1DBMSC ratio specifically for SFDBMSC and ICDBMSC systems. Monocytes (THP-1) were also co-cultured with DBMSCs at ratios of 2.5:1, 5:1, 10:1, and 20:1 (THP-1:DBMSC), and with HUVEC at similar ratios. Experiments were primarily conducted over 48 hours, with effects often measured at 24, 48, and 72 hours. Mitomycin C at 25 µg/ml was used to inhibit cell proliferation in some experiments. No specific dose-response comparisons for DBMSCs were explicitly reported for all measured effects.

analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Endothelial cells (HUVEC) and monocytes (THP-1) in co-culture

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly reduced (P < 0.05) adhesion of H2O2-treated monocytes to HUVEC after culturing with H2O2-untreated (UDBMSC) or H2O2-pretreated (TDBMSC) DBMSCs, indicating an inhibitory effect on monocyte adhesion to endothelial cells.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Mediates cellular interactions and inflammatory responses; immune cell recruitment to sites of inflammation/injury.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: DBMSCs co-culture in the presence of H2O2, mitigating monocyte adhesion to HUVEC.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a protective effect against inflammation and vascular damage by reducing monocyte infiltration, relevant for inflammatory diseases like atherosclerosis.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly reduced (P < 0.05) after 24, 48, and 72h pretreatment with 100 µM H2O2 as compared to untreated HUVEC.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cellular growth and division, essential for tissue repair and angiogenesis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: HUVEC pretreated with 100 µM H2O2 for 48h.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates endothelial cell damage or impaired regenerative capacity due to oxidative stress.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased (P < 0.05) in response to all examined concentrations of CMDBMSC or only at a high ratio of DBMSCs to HUVEC (1:1) in co-culture, as compared to untreated HUVEC.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cellular growth and division, essential for tissue repair and angiogenesis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: HUVEC cultured with CMDBMSC or co-cultured with DBMSCs (1:1 ratio).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates promotion of endothelial cell growth by soluble factors or direct contact with DBMSCs.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: HUVEC Proliferation (modulatory effect of DBMSCs in H2O2 environment)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: CMDBMSC significantly reduced (P < 0.05) HUVEC proliferation (vs H2O2 alone); SFDBMSC significantly increased (P < 0.05) HUVEC proliferation after 48 and 72 h (vs H2O2 alone); ICDBMSC did not significantly affect (P > 0.05) HUVEC proliferation, when compared to HUVEC pretreated with H2O2.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cellular growth and division, essential for tissue repair and angiogenesis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: HUVEC pretreated with 100 µM H2O2 and co-cultured with different forms of DBMSCs (CMDBMSC, SFDBMSC, ICDBMSC).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Suggests complex and varied effects of different DBMSC co-culture methods on HUVEC proliferation in an oxidative environment.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased (P < 0.05) by H2O2-treated monocytes (1HUVEC:10THP-1 + H2O2); this stimulatory effect was significantly reduced (P < 0.05) by monocytes pretreated with DBMSCs and H2O2 (THP-1/DBMSC + H2O2).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indirect regulation of endothelial cell growth by immune cells; cell growth and division; inhibition of excessive proliferation prevents pathology.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: HUVEC cultured in 100 µM H2O2 and exposed to monocytes, with or without DBMSC pretreatment of monocytes.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates H2O2-treated monocytes stimulate HUVEC proliferation, and DBMSCs can attenuate this pro-proliferative effect, suggesting a protective role against pathological cell growth, which contributes to atheroma plaque formation in atherosclerosis.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: H2O2 (100 µM) significantly reduced HUVEC migration (P < 0.05) compared to untreated. CMDBMSC alone had no significant effect, while ICDBMSC alone significantly increased migration (P < 0.05) compared to untreated HUVEC. In the presence of H2O2, CMDBMSC maintained reduced migration (P < 0.05 vs untreated), whereas SFDBMSC and ICDBMSC reversed H2O2's inhibitory effect, restoring migration to basal levels (P > 0.05 vs untreated) and significantly increasing it (P < 0.05) compared to H2O2-treated HUVEC alone.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Directed cell movement, essential for wound healing, angiogenesis, and immune responses.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: HUVEC exposed to 100 µM H2O2 and/or co-cultured with different forms of DBMSCs (CMDBMSC, SFDBMSC, ICDBMSC).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates impaired endothelial cell repair and angiogenic capacity due to oxidative stress, which can be modulated by DBMSCs, with SFDBMSC and ICDBMSC showing protective/restorative effects on migration. Dysfunctional migration contributes to atherosclerosis development.

analyzed_biomarkers.biomarker_name: Endothelial cell gene expression (e.g., survival, apoptosis, inflammation, adhesion, angiogenesis)
analyzed_biomarkers.measured_tissue_or_fluid: Human umbilical cord vein endothelial cells (HUVEC)
analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Gene Transcript Level / Protein Level (expression of adhesion molecules)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: DBMSCs modified the expression of many genes. Specifically, they induced genes mediating endothelial cell survival, Endothelin-1, Sphingosine kinase 1, Heme oxygenase-1, and various antiangiogenic genes. Conversely, DBMSCs reduced the expression of genes triggering apoptosis, injury, and inflammation, as well as proangiogenic genes. ICDBMSC also reduced endothelial cell expression of VCAM. No specific quantitative data for individual genes or fold changes were provided, beyond 'modified', 'induced', or 'reduced'.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Regulation of various endothelial cell processes including viability, inflammation, adhesion, and angiogenesis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: DBMSCs co-culture under the influence of H2O2, protecting endothelial cells from oxidative stress-induced damage.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a broad regulatory impact of DBMSCs on endothelial cell health and function in an oxidative stress environment, promoting survival, reducing inflammation, modulating adhesion, and influencing angiogenesis, which is significant for inflammatory diseases and atherosclerosis.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Activity decreased from a baseline of 77.5 ± 4.87 mU/mL to 29.50 ± 2.55 mU/mL after 100 µM H2O2 exposure for 48h. DBMSCs significantly increased activity in H2O2-treated HUVEC: CMDBMSC to 56.90 ± 3.11 mU/mL (1.92-fold increase), SFDBMSC to 62.38 ± 3.01 mU/mL (2.11-fold increase), and ICDBMSC to 65.49 ± 3.95 mU/mL (2.22-fold increase) compared to H2O2-treated HUVEC alone (all P < 0.05).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Key antioxidant enzyme, crucial for maintaining cellular redox balance by reducing oxidized glutathione and protecting cells from oxidative stress.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: HUVEC exposed to 100 µM H2O2, and then co-cultured with different forms of DBMSCs (CMDBMSC, SFDBMSC, ICDBMSC).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates oxidative stress impairs antioxidant defense, while DBMSCs enhance this defense, thereby protecting endothelial cells from oxidative damage, which is relevant for inflammatory diseases like atherosclerosis.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Baseline activity was 91.67 ± 10.14 mU/10^6 cell, reduced to 43.33 ± 10.73 mU/10^6 cell after H2O2 exposure. In H2O2-treated HUVEC, DBMSCs significantly increased activity (P < 0.05): CMDBMSC to 79.33 ± 7.21 mU/10^6 cell (1.83-fold increase), SFDBMSC to 88.33 ± 9.28 mU/10^6 cell (2.03-fold increase), and ICDBMSC to 83.33 ± 9.28 mU/10^6 cell (1.92-fold increase) compared to H2O2-treated HUVEC alone.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Critical antioxidant enzyme involved in maintaining cellular redox state, protein function, and protecting cells from oxidative stress.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: HUVEC exposed to 100 µM H2O2, and then co-cultured with different forms of DBMSCs (CMDBMSC, SFDBMSC, ICDBMSC).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates enhanced antioxidant defense mechanisms in endothelial cells, contributing to protection against oxidative injury, relevant for inflammatory diseases.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: H2O2 (100 µM) significantly increased HUVEC adhesion (P < 0.05) compared to untreated. In the presence of H2O2, CMDBMSC showed no significant change compared to H2O2-treated HUVEC; SFDBMSC significantly increased adhesion (P < 0.05) compared to H2O2-treated HUVEC; ICDBMSC significantly reduced adhesion (P < 0.05) compared to H2O2-treated HUVEC.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cell-to-surface or cell-to-cell binding, crucial for tissue integrity, inflammation, and atherosclerosis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: HUVEC pretreated with 100 µM H2O2 for 48h, and then co-cultured with different forms of DBMSCs (CMDBMSC, SFDBMSC, ICDBMSC).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates altered endothelial cell surface properties in response to oxidative stress and complex modulation by DBMSCs, with ICDBMSC showing a protective effect against H2O2-induced adhesion, which is relevant for inflammatory diseases like atherosclerosis.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased (P < 0.05) after 24h culture with DBMSCs (at all examined ratios), either alone or in the presence of H2O2, as compared to monocytes cultured alone or with H2O2. However, the addition of H2O2 to monocytes cultured with DBMSCs did not significantly change proliferation compared to monocytes cultured with H2O2 alone (P > 0.05).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cellular growth and division of immune cells.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Monocytes cultured with DBMSCs, with or without 100 µM H2O2.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates DBMSCs promote monocyte proliferation, and this stimulatory effect is not further enhanced by H2O2.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased (P < 0.05) after 24h pretreatment with 100 µM H2O2. Furthermore, it was significantly increased (P < 0.05) in H2O2-treated monocytes cultured with DBMSCs, compared to H2O2-treated monocytes alone.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cell adhesion molecule, critical for leukocyte recruitment and inflammatory responses.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Monocytes pretreated with 100 µM H2O2, and then cultured with DBMSCs.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates H2O2 promotes an inflammatory phenotype in monocytes, increasing their adhesive potential, and DBMSCs further augment this effect.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significantly increased (P < 0.05) in 100 µM H2O2-treated monocytes compared to untreated. However, there was no significant difference in CD44 expression between H2O2-treated monocytes and H2O2-treated monocytes cultured with DBMSCs.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cell adhesion molecule and receptor for hyaluronic acid, involved in cell migration, proliferation, and differentiation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Monocytes pretreated with 100 µM H2O2, with or without co-culture with DBMSCs.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates H2O2 promotes an inflammatory or activated phenotype in monocytes, but DBMSCs do not significantly alter this specific adhesion molecule's expression in H2O2-treated monocytes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: H2O2 (100 µM) exposure did not significantly change VCAM-1 expression in monocytes compared to untreated (P > 0.05, despite inconsistent text stating 'P < 0.05'). However, in H2O2-treated monocytes cultured with DBMSCs, VCAM-1 expression was significantly decreased (P < 0.05) compared to H2O2-treated monocytes alone.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Cell adhesion molecule, mediating leukocyte-endothelial interactions during inflammation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Monocytes pretreated with 100 µM H2O2, and then cultured with DBMSCs.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates DBMSCs can reduce VCAM-1 expression in H2O2-treated monocytes, potentially mitigating inflammatory cell adhesion and infiltration.
